text:
meena: hitting a pretty confusing bug in the Ruby SDK quickstart. When a long SSE stream is resumed after token rotate we sometimes see out-of-order chunks: part of event N appears after event N+1. Seems tied to reconnect timing + proxy buffering.

carlos: out-of-order? that's annoying. do you have a packet capture or logs of the chunks?

meena: yes, minimal example attached in GH issue. Raw fragments (proxy capture):
```
# initial stream
chunk1: "id: 501
event: chunk
data: first-half-

"
chunk2: "id: 502
event: chunk
data: full-second

"
# client times out and reconnects with Last-Event-ID: 501
# proxy drains/flushes buffers oddly
chunk3 (resume): "data: -second-half
id: 503
event: chunk
data: third

"
```
If the client naively concatenates buffered partials it assembles: event 501 data: first-half-data: -second-half which is fine, but if chunk3 with id 503 arrives before the buffered partial is flushed it can be emitted ahead of 502 -> reorder.

tayla: sounds like two separate problems: (A) partial buffer flush ordering; (B) concurrent resume attempts delivering events out-of-order. Ruby SDK uses a goroutine/thread-per-connection style and we do allow overlapping reconnect attempts when auth refresh takes longer.

meena: correct. In my run the auth refresh took ~220ms, the reconnect started, but an earlier pending read completed and pushed an extra chunk that then got processed after the resumed chunks. Reordering visible to app.

carlos: JS and Python SDKs both implemented a simple serial reconnect lock to ensure only one resume attempt runs. Do we have parity in Ruby?

meena: not yet. Ruby has optimistic reconnects. Proposed fixes: 1) add a per-client reconnect mutex so reconnections serialize; 2) when reconnecting with Last-Event-ID, snapshot last_seen_id and drop/ignore any frames with id <= snapshot; 3) on resume flush partial buffer and treat incoming chunk boundaries defensively (treat any new line starting with id: as a strong boundary).

qa: will add tests. Two corner cases to cover: server resends a suffix that duplicates the trailing partial (should be dedupable by id), and proxy reorders deliver where a buffered chunk from the old connection arrives after the new connection's chunks.

meena: edge case: some servers don't include id headers on every event. We need to fallback to sequence tickets (we have per-request sequence numbers) or hash(data) to detect duplicates. But don't want to rely on hashing for normal path.

carlos: another pragmatic mitigation: give sample apps an increased default read_timeout (60s) to reduce frequency of mid-stream reconnects for new users. Also document known limitations in SDK parity matrix.

infra-bot: ci: build #2026.06.01-18 failing flakes: ruby_sse_reorder_test.rb (2/50 runs) - rerun requested. https://ci.redwood.example/2026/06/01/18

meena: I'll open a small PR implementing the reconnect mutex + id-based filtering + flush-on-resume for Ruby. Will include a comment linking to the Go/Python parity PRs.

qa: after PR please run the race harness we use in infra (50 clients, random auth delays, 1-5ms chunk splits). Also include a deterministic unit test that simulates an "old" chunk arriving after the resume.

carlos: can infra team add a proxy-mode test variant that flips chunk order occasionally? That will help find regressions.

meena: yep, filing infra test request. Will ping once PR is up. Thanks folks. :)
